correctness.rationale: The code is exactly the kernel of the fixed rank-nine Petersen vertex-edge incidence map. Its 512 syndromes are all even vertex subsets, and every binary error support is one of 32768 edge masks. The supplied verifier exhausts them to obtain each minimum weight and multiplicity; independently it performs BFS in the 512-syndrome graph and checks shortest path counts equal factorial(distance) times minimizing edge-support count. The 120 natural S5 automorphisms partition all 512 syndromes into 18 disjoint explicitly listed orbits and preserve the checked statistics. The orbit certificate sums to the full bivariate enumerator; the unique depth-five all-ones syndrome has six leaders, exactly the six perfect matchings. All arithmetic is exact and no inference from finite sampling to infinite cases is made.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the full joint minimum-distance/leader-multiplicity distribution across every one of the 512 binary Petersen cycle-code cosets and its 18 orbit certificate, not the construction, weight enumerator, T-join equivalence, or covering radius in isolation. The initiating 2026 full-text graph-code paper, Section 6.2, exhibits a [15,6,5] generator matrix but no coset table, syndrome search, or nearest-leader counts. Brouwer lists only codeword weights and the Error Correction Zoo describes the known code. The 1993 Solé–Zaslavsky paper covers cycle-code radius and minimum T-joins; only its abstract/index and searchable fragments were accessible, which creates material residual risk but provide no evidence of a 512-coset bivariate enumerator. Searches of equivalent terms and published mathematical records found no dominator. Prior coding facts are credited; remaining older-table risk is explicit.

The radius, code construction, automorphism group, perfect-matching count, and ordinary weight enumerator are known facts; novelty is asserted only for their new combined exact bivariate coset table.

value.rationale: For minimum-distance decoding, syndrome weight alone or even coset distance does not determine the number of equally good corrections. The 18-orbit bivariate census gives a complete exact ambiguity profile on all 512 syndromes of a canonical highly symmetric [15,6,5] graph code, including unequal multiplicities 1–6 and a unique six-way ambiguous deep coset. It is a natural finite coding invariant motivated by recent graph-code literature and useful as a reproducible decoding benchmark. Though no new all-graphs theorem is claimed, the complete finite classification is not a one-off arbitrary parameter slice nor a restatement of known codeword weights.
